The package singleton is BRGRenderer (accessed via BRGRenderer.Instance). There are two entry points for registering instances: subclass BRGRegisterer (MonoBehaviour) or use BRGRegistrationTracker directly (non-MonoBehaviour). This doc points you at authoritative source and docs rather than duplicating them — read the linked files for full detail. Where to look All paths below are inside the BRGInstancedRenderer package folder in the Unity project. What you need Read Tracker API + struct shapes (InstanceData, InstanceLink, ChunkLink, RenderSignature) Runtime/Scripts/Registerers/BRGRegistrationTracker.cs (its MonoBehaviour wrapper lives in Runtime/Scripts/Registerers/BRGRegisterer.cs) MonoBehaviour subclass API + protected forwarders Runtime/Scripts/Registerers/BRGRegisterer.cs Singleton (BRGRenderer) full API Runtime/Scripts/Core/BRGInstancedRenderer.cs + partials (.Batches.cs, .Chunks.cs, .Culling.cs, .Debug.cs, .HZB.cs, .Prototypes.cs, .SpeedTree.cs, .Upload.cs) Working custom-registerer example (uses Stage* patterns) Examples/Scripts/BRGRegistererExample.cs Per-instance color via InstanceLink on a real terrain (uses GetInstanceLink + *Unsafe) Examples/Scripts/TreeRandomColor.cs Reference terrain implementation Runtime/Scripts/Registerers/Terrain/TerrainBRGRegisterer.cs + .Trees.cs / .Details.cs / .Details.Extraction.cs partials Reference GameObject-group implementation (kept-source, transform-tracked) Runtime/Scripts/Registerers/GameObjects/BRGGameObjectGroup.cs Reference baked-instance group implementation (destroyed-source, packed blob) Runtime/Scripts/Registerers/Baked/BRGInstanceGroup.cs + .Bake.cs Config schema (every serialized field + tooltips) Runtime/Scripts/Config/BRGInstancedRendererConfig.cs Per-prototype shadow / LOD / density overrides Runtime/Scripts/Config/BRGPrototypeExtraData.cs Per-group runtime LOD bias + density control (ScriptableObject) Runtime/Scripts/Config/BRGPrototypeGroup.cs Unity 6.2+ Mesh LOD setup Runtime/Scripts/Config/BRGMeshLodData.cs Per-camera LOD bias and crossfade snap Runtime/Scripts/Config/BRGCameraSettings.cs Terrain detail prototype override Runtime/Scripts/Registerers/Terrain/BRGTerrainDetailOverride.cs Non-obvious concepts These are not visible from reading any single file. State them explicitly to avoid generating wrong code. The singleton class is BRGRenderer, not BRGInstancedRenderer. Access it via BRGRenderer.Instance. A chunk holds a mix of any number of render signatures. Chunks are not per-signature. A pool also holds a mix of any number of render signatures. Pools are fixed-size GPU memory blocks of 64 instance slots each (hard-coded — not configurable). A prototype index is the global handle returned by RegisterRenderSignature*. A RenderSignature is the full data (asset + render config). These are different things. Instances spatially overlapping with a chunk don't have to belong to it. Each instance belongs to exactly one chunk, but multiple chunks can spatially overlap. Spatially large chunks are fine. Chunk culling is an optimization, not a requirement — culling a few extra instances that survive chunk-level culling is cheap on the GPU. InstanceLink is a passive handle (just ChunkId + GlobalBRGSlotIndex). All per-instance mutation lives on the tracker/registerer via Stage* or *Unsafe methods — there are no methods directly on InstanceLink. ChunkLink carries an ABA-safe generation counter. Use ChunkLink.IsAlive (not just IsValid) before operating on a stored link. Overflow chunks are allocated automatically when WriteChunk or AddInstance exceeds MaxInstancesPerChunk. They share the primary's culling bounds. GetInstanceLink, GetTotalChunkInstanceCount, ReleaseChunk, and the ChunkWritten event all span primary + overflows transparently. The ChunkWritten event fires once per primary chunk after the primary AND all its overflow sub-chunks have completed their GPU writes. Use it to safely call GetInstanceLink after WriteChunk. WriteChunk is a one-shot bulk write. For runtime instance mutation use AddInstance / Stage* / *Unsafe. BRGRegistrationTracker is the non-MonoBehaviour entry point — wire InitializeCallback / ShutdownCallback for setup/teardown logic instead of subclassing. Using InstanceLinks An InstanceLink is the handle you pass to every per-instance modification call. It's just ChunkId + GlobalBRGSlotIndex — no methods on it directly. How to obtain one: Returned by AddInstance(chunk, instanceData) and AddInstances(chunk, array, count) when you grow a chunk one or many instances at a time. Returned by MoveInstanceToChunk(source, dest, instanceData) when moving between chunks. Looked up by logical index via GetInstanceLink(chunkLink, localIndex) — where localIndex is 0..GetTotalChunkInstanceCount(chunkLink) - 1 and spans primary + overflow chunks transparently. Use this for chunks populated by WriteChunk (not AddInstance), or any time you need the link for the Nth instance in a chunk. How to use one: pass to any Stage* or *Unsafe method on the tracker (or, inside a registerer subclass, on this). Examples: tracker.StageColor(link, color), tracker.SetPositionUnsafe(link, pos), tracker.StageRemove(link). Timing: WriteChunk does not necessarily complete its GPU upload on the same frame — the write can be deferred (e.g. for a buffer resize). Do not call GetInstanceLink immediately after WriteChunk and assume the link is valid; the slot indices aren't guaranteed to exist yet. Instead, grab links from inside the ChunkWritten event handler (or OnChunkWritten(int chunkId) override in a subclass), which fires once per primary chunk after primary + all overflow sub-chunks have finished writing. That's the only path that's guaranteed safe. If you really need a link before the callback fires, check link.IsValid before using it. Two reference patterns: Examples/Scripts/BRGRegistererExample.cs — stores InstanceLinks in a list as instances are added (AddInstance return value) and modifies them later with Stage* calls for batch updates. Examples/Scripts/TreeRandomColor.cs — sits next to a TerrainBRGRegisterer, subscribes to OnTreeChunkWritten, then uses Registration.GetInstanceLink(chunk, i) + Registration.SetColorUnsafe(link, color) to apply a one-shot random color per tree. Stage* vs *Unsafe There are two paths for modifying existing instances: Stage* — keeps a per-slot dictionary on the tracker. Repeated writes to the same slot (or to different fields of the same slot) are merged into a single entry, then bulk-uploaded to BRGRenderer when the tracker flushes each frame. Use this if your code might touch the same slot more than once per frame — dedup is handled for you. *Unsafe — bypasses the tracker and forwards each call directly to BRGRenderer. You must guarantee at most one write per slot per frame yourself. Two *Unsafe calls on the same slot in the same frame, or mixing Stage* and *Unsafe on the same slot, both produce undefined results. Default to Stage*. Only reach for *Unsafe in code paths where you've already deduplicated writes per slot. Public API surface Names only — do NOT infer signatures from names. Before calling any method, open the source file (see Where to look) and read its actual signature. Common pitfalls: AllocChunk() takes no arguments (bounds go in WriteChunk, not AllocChunk); WriteChunk(link, instances, bounds, cullDistance, instanceCullDistance) takes a ChunkLink and a NativeArray<InstanceData>, not a chunk id and a managed array; the InstanceData field is signatureIndex (not prototypeIndex). BRGRenderer (singleton, via BRGRenderer.Instance) Lifecycle: Instance, HasInstance, IsInitialized, Dispose, Shutdown, Reinitialize, RuntimeRefresh Registration: RegisterRenderSignatureFromPrefab, RegisterRenderSignaturesFromPrefab, RegisterRenderSignature, UnregisterRenderSignature, PurgeUnusedPrototypes, GetPrototype, GetPrototypeRefCount, GetPrototypeInstanceCount Chunks: AllocateChunk, WriteChunk, FreeChunk, IsChunkValid, GetChunkGeneration, GetChunkInstanceCount, GetChunkBounds, GetChunkPoolCount, GetChunkPoolIndex, GetPoolOccupancy, RecalculateChunkBounds, SetChunkEnabled, GetChunkEnabled Direct instance modification: SetInstancePosition, SetInstanceRotation, SetInstanceScale, MoveAndRotateInstance, MoveInstance, SetInstanceColor, SetInstanceEnabled, IsInstanceEnabled, SampleInstanceLightProbe, AddInstance, AppendInstances, RemoveInstance Buffer / memory: CompactBuffers, ShiftInstances, FlushStagedUploads, GetMemoryBreakdown, AllocatedBufferMemory Crossfade / probes: SnapAllCrossfadeStates, SnapCrossfadeState, CrossfadeTimeScale, ResampleAllLightProbes (runtime density and LOD-bias scaling are now per-group via BRGPrototypeGroup, not on the singleton) BRGRegistrationTracker (non-MonoBehaviour entry point) Lifecycle: Initialize, Shutdown, InitializeCallback, ShutdownCallback, BRGSystem, IsRegistered, Name Events: ChunkWritten Registration: ExtractRenderSignature, RegisterRenderSignatureFromPrefab, RegisterRenderSignaturesFromPrefab, RegisterRenderSignature, UnregisterRenderSignature Chunks: MaxInstancesPerChunk, AllocChunk, WriteChunk, ReleaseChunk, RecalculateChunkBounds, SetChunkEnabled, GetChunkEnabled, SetRenderEnabled Instance lifecycle: AddInstance, AddInstances, MoveInstanceToChunk Lookups: GetInstanceLink, GetTotalChunkInstanceCount, GetOverflowChunkCount, GetPerChunkInstanceCounts Staged writes: StagePosition, StageRotation, StageScale, StageMoveAndRotate, StageMove, StageColor, StageSetEnabled, StageRemove Unsafe direct writes: SetPositionUnsafe, SetRotationUnsafe, SetScaleUnsafe, MoveAndRotateUnsafe, MoveUnsafe, SetColorUnsafe, SetEnabledUnsafe, RemoveUnsafe, SampleLightProbeUnsafe BRGRegisterer (MonoBehaviour subclass entry point) Implement: OnInitialize, OnShutdown (abstract); OnChunkWritten(int chunkId) (virtual) Lifecycle: Initialize, Shutdown, Registration (the underlying tracker) Protected (for use inside your subclass): all tracker methods above for registration / chunks / instance lifecycle / lookups Public (also callable from outside): SetChunkEnabled, GetChunkEnabled, SetRenderEnabled, all Stage* and *Unsafe methods Components users add in the editor BRGInstancedRendererConfig — singleton config asset (auto-created at Assets/BRGInstancedRenderer/BRGIRConfig.asset, auto-added to Preloaded Assets) BRGGameObjectGroup + BRGGameObjectLink — GameObject batch conversion with native transform tracking (source GameObjects kept, renderers disabled) BRGInstanceGroup — alternative baked path that destroys the source GameObjects after baking, storing transforms + render signatures on the component. Smaller storage, zero per-instance GameObject overhead, no automatic transform tracking. Bake() / ExpandToGameObjects() editor methods, IsBaked / InstanceCount / PrototypeCount runtime properties. TerrainBRGRegisterer + BRGTerrainDetailOverride — terrain tree/detail registration with optional LOD-group detail prototypes BRGPrototypeExtraData — per-prefab shadow cascade / shadow LOD / density / screen-size / LOD-fade overrides; also carries the optional prototypeGroup reference BRGPrototypeGroup — ScriptableObject identity token for runtime LOD bias and density control. Replaces the removed BRGRenderer.SetGlobalDensity. SetLodBias(float) and SetDensity(float) apply to every prototype that references the group; values are runtime-only (default 1) and not serialized — re-apply each session BRGMeshLodData — Unity 6.2+ Mesh LOD level config (alternative to LOD Groups) BRGCameraSettings — per-camera LOD bias multiplier and SnapCrossfade() Footguns In OnShutdown(), clear only local state. The base class frees chunks and unregisters prototypes automatically — don't do it yourself or you'll double-free. Don't call BRGRenderer.Instance.AllocateChunk / FreeChunk / RegisterRenderSignature directly from inside a registerer subclass. Use the inherited protected wrappers (AllocChunk, ReleaseChunk, RegisterRenderSignatureFromPrefab, etc.) so the base class can track them for automatic cleanup. After WriteChunk, don't assume GetInstanceLink will return valid handles on the same call — the GPU write may be deferred. Subscribe to ChunkWritten (or override OnChunkWritten in your subclass) and call GetInstanceLink from there. A stored ChunkLink can go stale if the chunk was freed elsewhere. Use ChunkLink.IsAlive (which checks generation against BRGRenderer's current state) before mutating through it, not just IsValid. For per-camera operations (e.g. snap crossfade after a teleport on one specific camera), add a BRGCameraSettings component to that camera or call BRGRenderer.Instance.SnapCrossfadeState(camera). SnapAllCrossfadeStates() covers every camera at once. Pool size is hard-coded to 64. Don't try to configure it. Max Pools Per Chunk in the config controls how many pools a chunk may hold (= max instances per chunk). Stage* and *Unsafe cannot be safely used on the same slot in the same frame, and *Unsafe cannot be used twice on the same slot in the same frame either. See the Stage* vs *Unsafe section above. Closing If you need something not covered here, read the source in Runtime/Scripts/ (it's the authoritative truth). This file is just a router — when in doubt, open the file and read it.

articles/api/core-methods.html.title: Core Methods | BRG Instanced Renderer
articles/api/core-methods.html.summary: Core Methods Public methods on the BRGRenderer singleton for runtime control. Access the singleton via BRGRenderer.Instance. For runtime LOD bias and density scaling per prototype group, see BRG Prototype Group. The old singleton-level SetGlobalDensity has been replaced by BRGPrototypeGroup.SetDensity(). CrossfadeTimeScale public float CrossfadeTimeScale { get; set; } Multiplier applied to animated crossfade delta time. Default is 1f. Higher values speed up transitions, lower values slow them down. Clamped to ≥ 0. The main use case is fast camera movement — when the camera moves quickly through the scene, instances cross LOD thresholds rapidly and a slow crossfade can become visible as visible popping. Increasing CrossfadeTimeScale shortens the transitions so they finish before the camera has moved far enough for the change to be noticeable. You can also set it to 0 to pause crossfades entirely (e.g. while the game is paused). // speed up crossfades during fast camera movement BRGRenderer.Instance.CrossfadeTimeScale = 2f; // restore default BRGRenderer.Instance.CrossfadeTimeScale = 1f; // pause crossfades BRGRenderer.Instance.CrossfadeTimeScale = 0f; RuntimeRefresh public void RuntimeRefresh() A faster refresh path for use at runtime. Shuts down and re-initializes all active registerers, causing them to re-extract and re-upload their instance data. Use this after you have programmatically changed terrain data, swapped prefabs, or modified prototype settings at runtime. BRGRenderer.Instance.RuntimeRefresh(); CompactBuffers public void CompactBuffers() Compacts the internal instance pool and chunk buffers to reduce GPU memory waste. Leaves approximately 25% headroom above current usage. This causes a small frame hitch, so call it during pauses, loading screens, or scene transitions rather than during gameplay. // compact during a loading screen BRGRenderer.Instance.CompactBuffers(); The Config also provides an Enable Auto Compaction option that runs compaction automatically when utilization is low, but manual compaction is recommended to prevent hitches. SnapAllCrossfadeStates public void SnapAllCrossfadeStates() Snap all crossfade animations to their target LODs for all cameras. Call after teleportation or scene load to prevent a mass fade-in of all visible instances. // after teleporting the player player.transform.position = newPosition; BRGRenderer.Instance.SnapAllCrossfadeStates(); SnapCrossfadeState public bool SnapCrossfadeState(Camera camera) public bool SnapCrossfadeState(int viewID) Snap animated crossfade for a single camera or view. Returns false if the view has not been seen by the culling system yet. The Camera overload is a convenience wrapper that passes camera.GetInstanceID() to the int overload. Parameter Type Description camera Camera The camera to snap crossfade for. viewID int The view identifier (camera instance ID or shadow view ID). Returns Description bool true if the view was found and snapped, false if the view ID is unknown. // snap crossfade for a specific camera after teleporting it BRGRenderer.Instance.SnapCrossfadeState(myCamera); PurgeUnusedPrototypes public int PurgeUnusedPrototypes() Immediately remove all prototypes with a reference count of zero, bypassing the Prototype Idle Grace Period on the Config. Returns the number of prototypes purged. By default, unused prototypes stay alive for the grace period (default 30s) so that re-registering the same prefab during a scene transition reuses the existing GPU data with zero work. Call this method only when you want to reclaim GPU memory immediately — for example, during a memory-tight loading screen. int purged = BRGRenderer.Instance.PurgeUnusedPrototypes(); Debug.Log($"Purged {purged} unused prototypes"); ResampleAllLightProbes public void ResampleAllLightProbes() Force a re-sample of legacy light probes for every active instance. Only relevant when Support Legacy Light Probes is enabled on the Config. Call this after Adaptive Probe Volumes or legacy probes are rebaked at runtime, otherwise existing instances continue using their last sampled values. LightmapSettings.lightProbes = newProbeData; BRGRenderer.Instance.ResampleAllLightProbes(); ShiftInstances public void ShiftInstances(Vector3 offset) Shift all instance positions and chunk bounds by an offset. Designed for floating world origin systems that periodically re-center the world to avoid floating-point precision issues at large coordinates. This only shifts the BRG data — you are responsible for shifting GameObjects, terrain, cameras, and any other world-space objects separately. Parameter Type Description offset Vector3 World-space offset to apply to all instances and chunk bounds. // re-center the world around the player Vector3 shift = -player.transform.position; BRGRenderer.Instance.ShiftInstances(shift); // shift everything else too player.transform.position += shift; // ... shift terrain, cameras, etc.

articles/api/custom-registerer.html.title: Custom Registerer | BRG Instanced Renderer
articles/api/custom-registerer.html.summary: Custom Registerer Before reading this page, make sure you've read System Overview to understand how prototypes, render signatures, chunks, and pools work together. BRGRegisterer is an abstract MonoBehaviour base class for building your own instance registration components. It wraps a BRGRegistrationTracker internally, which handles the BRG singleton lifecycle, prototype reference counting, chunk tracking with automatic cleanup, overflow management, and editor support — so your subclass only needs to focus on what to register and where. For non-MonoBehaviour usage (ECS, static managers, etc.), use BRGRegistrationTracker directly. Both built-in registerers (BRG GameObject Group and BRG Terrain Registerer) extend this class. For a working example, see Registerer Example. Creating a Custom Registerer Extend BRGRegisterer and implement two methods: using Unity.Collections; using Unity.Mathematics; using UnityEngine; namespace BRGInstancedRenderer { public class MyRegisterer : BRGRegisterer { [SerializeField] GameObject _prefab; int _protoIndex = -1; ChunkLink _chunk; protected override void OnInitialize() { // 1. Register your render signature _protoIndex = RegisterRenderSignatureFromPrefab(_prefab); if (_protoIndex < 0) return; // 2. Allocate a chunk _chunk = AllocChunk(); if (!_chunk.IsValid) return; // 3. Build instance data var instances = new NativeArray<InstanceData>(100, Allocator.TempJob); for (int i = 0; i < 100; i++) { instances[i] = new InstanceData { position = new float3(i * 2f, 0f, 0f), rotation = quaternion.identity, scale = new float3(1f), signatureIndex = _protoIndex, color = new Color32(255, 255, 255, 255) }; } // 4. Write to the chunk var bounds = new Bounds(Vector3.zero, new Vector3(200f, 10f, 10f)); WriteChunk(_chunk, instances, bounds); instances.Dispose(); } protected override void OnShutdown() { // Clean up local state only. // Do NOT free chunks or unregister render signatures - the base class does that. _chunk = ChunkLink.Invalid; _protoIndex = -1; } } } The base class automatically: Acquires the BRGRenderer singleton Calls OnInitialize() on enable, OnShutdown() on disable Frees all chunks allocated via AllocChunk() on shutdown Unregisters all render signatures registered via RegisterRenderSignatureFromPrefab() on shutdown Handles editor lifecycle ([ExecuteAlways] with deferred initialization) Structs See BRGRegistrationTracker / Structs for full documentation of InstanceData, PrototypeData, RenderSignature, ChunkLink, and InstanceLink. Properties Property Access Type Description BRGSystem protected BRGRenderer Reference to the singleton. Set before OnInitialize() is called, cleared after OnShutdown() returns. Use it freely during those methods. Registration public BRGRegistrationTracker The underlying tracker. Created lazily on first access — available before Initialize(). _registered protected bool true while the registerer is initialized. Check this before performing operations. Manual Lifecycle By default, BRGRegisterer initializes on OnEnable and shuts down on OnDisable. If you need manual control (e.g., a button-driven workflow), override OnEnable/OnDisable and call these methods directly: Method Description void Initialize() Acquire the singleton and call OnInitialize(). Safe to call multiple times — does nothing if already registered. void Shutdown() Call OnShutdown(), free all tracked chunks and prototypes, and release the singleton. See the Registerer Example for a working example of manual lifecycle using _autoRegister. API These methods are forwarded to the underlying BRGRegistrationTracker. For full descriptions of each method (parameters, edge cases, etc.), see the BRGRegistrationTracker page. Lifecycle methods (Register*, AllocChunk, WriteChunk, ReleaseChunk, AddInstance*, Get*, and the OnChunkWritten callback) are protected — intended to be used from within your subclass. Visibility controls (SetChunkEnabled, SetRenderEnabled) and the Stage* / *Unsafe modification methods are public, so other code can drive instance updates after the registerer is initialized. Render Signature Registration Method Description RenderSignature ExtractRenderSignature(GameObject) Extract without registering — useful for modifying settings before registration. int RegisterRenderSignatureFromPrefab(GameObject) Register a single signature from a prefab. Tracked. int[] RegisterRenderSignaturesFromPrefab(GameObject) Register multiple signatures from a multi-renderer prefab. Tracked. int RegisterRenderSignature(RenderSignature) Register an explicit signature. Tracked. void UnregisterRenderSignature(int globalIdx) Manually unregister a prototype. Chunk Management Method Description int MaxInstancesPerChunk Maximum instances per chunk (driven by Max Pools Per Chunk × 64). ChunkLink AllocChunk() Allocate a new chunk. Tracked. void WriteChunk(ChunkLink, NativeArray<InstanceData>, Bounds, float cullDistance, float instanceCullDistance) Write instances. Auto-overflows. void ReleaseChunk(ChunkLink) Free a chunk and all its overflows. void RecalculateChunkBounds(ChunkLink, Bounds) Update chunk culling bounds. void SetChunkEnabled(ChunkLink, bool) Enable/disable a chunk for rendering. bool GetChunkEnabled(ChunkLink) Check chunk enabled state. void SetRenderEnabled(bool) Enable/disable rendering for ALL chunks this registerer owns. Instance Lifecycle Method Description InstanceLink AddInstance(ChunkLink, InstanceData) Add a single instance, with automatic overflow. InstanceLink[] AddInstances(ChunkLink, NativeArray<InstanceData>, int count) Add multiple. InstanceLink MoveInstanceToChunk(InstanceLink source, ChunkLink dest, InstanceData) Move between chunks. Lookups Method Description InstanceLink GetInstanceLink(ChunkLink, int localIndex) Resolve a logical index (spanning primary + overflow) into a current InstanceLink. int GetTotalChunkInstanceCount(ChunkLink) Sum across primary + overflow chunks. int GetOverflowChunkCount(ChunkLink) Number of overflow chunks attached. void GetPerChunkInstanceCounts(ChunkLink, List<int>) Counts per sub-chunk. Tracked Staging The Stage* methods buffer per-slot writes and merge updates to the same instance within a frame into a single GPU write. This is the recommended path for runtime modifications. See Tracked Staging for the full list. Both InstanceLink and int globalSlot overloads are provided for every staging method. Unsafe Direct Modification The *Unsafe methods skip the staging buffer and write directly to BRGRenderer. Use only when you've already deduplicated writes yourself or need writes to land immediately. See Unsafe Direct Modification. Mixing staged and unsafe writes on the same slot within a frame is undefined — pick one path per slot. Callbacks Method Description virtual void OnChunkWritten(int chunkId) Override to react when a primary chunk and all of its overflows have finished writing to GPU. Useful for caching InstanceLink handles after WriteChunk. Notes Always use RegisterRenderSignature* / AllocChunk / ReleaseChunk instead of calling BRGSystem.RegisterPrototype / BRGSystem.AllocateChunk / BRGSystem.FreeChunk directly. The base class tracks these for automatic cleanup. Do not free chunks or unregister prototypes in OnShutdown(). The base class handles all BRG resource cleanup after OnShutdown() returns. The BRGSystem property is set before OnInitialize() and cleared after OnShutdown(). Use it freely during those methods. BRGRegisterer is marked [ExecuteAlways], so it works in the editor outside of play mode. When a WriteChunk exceeds MaxInstancesPerChunk, overflow chunks are allocated automatically and share the primary chunk's bounds. All queries (GetInstanceLink, GetTotalChunkInstanceCount, etc.) span primary + overflows transparently.

articles/api/direct-api.html.title: Direct API | BRG Instanced Renderer
articles/api/direct-api.html.summary: Direct API In most cases, you should use a BRGRegistrationTracker or Custom Registerer instead of calling these methods directly. They handle prototype reference counting, chunk tracking, overflow management, and automatic cleanup. Calling the raw API means you are responsible for all of that yourself — failing to unregister prototypes or free chunks will leak GPU memory. The direct API is available on the BRGRenderer singleton via BRGRenderer.Instance. These are the same methods that BRGRegistrationTracker calls internally. Singleton Member Description static BRGRenderer Instance Get or create the singleton. Auto-initializes on first access. static bool HasInstance Check if the singleton exists without creating it. bool IsInitialized Whether the system is initialized and ready. Prototype Registration Method Description int RegisterRenderSignatureFromPrefab(GameObject prefab) Register a render signature from a prefab. Returns the prototype index, or -1 on failure. Increments the reference count if already registered. int[] RegisterRenderSignaturesFromPrefab(GameObject prefab) Register multiple signatures from a prefab that produces more than one (e.g. multi-renderer prefabs). Returns the array of prototype indices. int RegisterRenderSignature(RenderSignature signature) Register a custom render signature. Deduplicates by asset identity hash + config hash. Returns the prototype index. bool UnregisterRenderSignature(int protoIndex) Decrement the reference count for a prototype. Returns true if the count reached zero. Zero-refcount prototypes are automatically purged after a grace period (default 30s, configurable via Prototype Idle Grace Period). If the prototype is re-registered before the grace period expires, it is reused without any GPU work. int PurgeUnusedPrototypes() Immediately remove all prototypes with a reference count of zero, bypassing the grace period. Returns the number purged. RenderSignature GetPrototype(int protoIndex) Get the render signature for a prototype index. int GetPrototypeRefCount(int protoIndex) Get the current reference count. Chunk Management Method Description int AllocateChunk() Allocate a new chunk. Returns the chunk ID. void WriteChunk(int chunkId, NativeArray<InstanceData> instances, Bounds bounds, float cullDistance = 0f, float instanceCullDistance = float.MaxValue) Write instances to a chunk. Bounds should tightly enclose all instances. cullDistance is a per-chunk distance cutoff (0 = unlimited). instanceCullDistance applies during GPU culling per-instance. void FreeChunk(int chunkId) Free a chunk and return its pools to the free list. bool IsChunkValid(int chunkId, int generation) ABA-safe liveness check. Use against a ChunkLink's stored generation to detect stale handles. int GetChunkGeneration(int chunkId) Get the current generation counter for a chunk slot. void RecalculateChunkBounds(int chunkId, Bounds newBounds) Update chunk culling bounds. Use after removals have made the original bounds too loose. void SetChunkEnabled(int chunkId, bool enabled) Enable or disable a chunk for rendering. int GetChunkInstanceCount(int chunkId) Get the number of instances in a chunk. int GetChunkPoolCount(int chunkId) Get the number of pools currently used by a chunk. int GetChunkPoolIndex(int chunkId, int poolLocalIdx) Get the global pool index for a chunk's local pool slot. Instance Addition & Removal Method Description int AddInstance(int chunkId, InstanceData instance) Add a single instance. Returns the global slot index, or -1 if the chunk is full. int AppendInstances(int chunkId, NativeArray<InstanceData> instances, int srcOffset, int count, NativeArray<int> outSlotIndices) Add multiple instances. Returns the number actually placed. Slot indices are written to outSlotIndices. void RemoveInstance(int chunkId, int globalSlotIndex) Remove an instance by slot index. Chunk bounds are not automatically recalculated. void SetInstanceEnabled(int globalSlotIndex, bool enabled) Enable or disable an instance. Disabled instances are invisible to culling but keep their slot and pool allocation. Instance Modification All modification methods take a global slot index and stage the change for GPU upload. Method Description void SetInstancePosition(int globalSlotIndex, float3 position) Set position only. void SetInstanceRotation(int globalSlotIndex, quaternion rotation) Set rotation only. void SetInstanceScale(int globalSlotIndex, float3 scale) Set scale only. void MoveAndRotateInstance(int globalSlotIndex, float3 position, quaternion rotation) Set position and rotation. void MoveInstance(int globalSlotIndex, float3 position, quaternion rotation, float3 scale) Set full TRS. Light probes are not re-sampled automatically. void SetInstanceColor(int globalSlotIndex, Color32 color) Set per-instance color. Requires Enable Per-Instance Color on the Config. void SampleInstanceLightProbe(int globalSlotIndex, float3 position) Re-sample light probes at a position. Call manually after moving an instance if using legacy light probes. Buffer & Memory Method Description void CompactBuffers() Compact GPU buffers to reduce memory waste. Leaves ~25% headroom. Causes a small hitch — call during loading screens or pauses. void ShiftInstances(Vector3 offset) Shift all instance positions and chunk bounds by an offset. For floating origin systems. You are responsible for shifting GameObjects, terrain, and cameras separately. void FlushStagedUploads() Force all staged GPU uploads to execute immediately. Normally called automatically before culling. long AllocatedBufferMemory Total allocated GPU buffer memory in bytes. Lifecycle Example using Unity.Collections; using Unity.Mathematics; using UnityEngine; namespace BRGInstancedRenderer { public class DirectAPIExample : MonoBehaviour { [SerializeField] GameObject _prefab; int _protoIndex = -1; int _chunkId = -1; void OnEnable() { var brg = BRGRenderer.Instance; // 1. Register prototype _protoIndex = brg.RegisterRenderSignatureFromPrefab(_prefab); if (_protoIndex < 0) return; // 2. Allocate chunk _chunkId = brg.AllocateChunk(); // 3. Build instance data var instances = new NativeArray<InstanceData>(100, Allocator.TempJob); for (int i = 0; i < 100; i++) { instances[i] = new InstanceData { position = new float3(i * 2f, 0f, 0f), rotation = quaternion.identity, scale = new float3(1f), signatureIndex = _protoIndex, color = new Color32(255, 255, 255, 255) }; } // 4. Write to chunk var bounds = new Bounds(Vector3.zero, new Vector3(200f, 10f, 10f)); brg.WriteChunk(_chunkId, instances, bounds); instances.Dispose(); } void OnDisable() { if (!BRGRenderer.HasInstance) return; var brg = BRGRenderer.Instance; // You must clean up manually if (_chunkId >= 0) { brg.FreeChunk(_chunkId); _chunkId = -1; } if (_protoIndex >= 0) { brg.UnregisterRenderSignature(_protoIndex); _protoIndex = -1; } } } } Compare this with the equivalent BRGRegistrationTracker or Custom Registerer version, which handle chunk freeing, overflow, and prototype unregistration automatically.

articles/api/registration-tracker.html.summary: BRGRegistrationTracker Before reading this page, make sure you've read System Overview to understand how prototypes, render signatures, chunks, and pools work together. BRGRegistrationTracker is the resource tracking layer that both BRGRegisterer and the built-in registerers use internally. It manages prototype reference counting, chunk tracking with automatic overflow, and full cleanup on shutdown — without requiring a GameObject. Use BRGRegistrationTracker directly when you need to manage BRG instances from a non-MonoBehaviour context (ECS systems, static managers, network callbacks, etc.). For MonoBehaviour-based registration, use Custom Registerer (BRGRegisterer) instead, which wraps a tracker with automatic OnEnable/OnDisable lifecycle. Creating a Tracker using Unity.Collections; using Unity.Mathematics; using UnityEngine; namespace BRGInstancedRenderer { public class MyManager { BRGRegistrationTracker _tracker; int _protoIndex = -1; ChunkLink _chunk; public void Start(GameObject prefab) { _tracker = new BRGRegistrationTracker("MyManager"); // Connect to BRGRenderer singleton if (!_tracker.Initialize()) return; // 1. Register render signature _protoIndex = _tracker.RegisterRenderSignatureFromPrefab(prefab); if (_protoIndex < 0) return; // 2. Allocate a chunk _chunk = _tracker.AllocChunk(); if (!_chunk.IsValid) return; // 3. Build instance data var instances = new NativeArray<InstanceData>(100, Allocator.TempJob); for (int i = 0; i < 100; i++) { instances[i] = new InstanceData { position = new float3(i * 2f, 0f, 0f), rotation = quaternion.identity, scale = new float3(1f), signatureIndex = _protoIndex, color = new Color32(255, 255, 255, 255) }; } // 4. Write to chunk var bounds = new Bounds(Vector3.zero, new Vector3(200f, 10f, 10f)); _tracker.WriteChunk(_chunk, instances, bounds); instances.Dispose(); } public void Stop() { // Frees all chunks, unregisters all prototypes, disconnects from BRGRenderer _tracker?.Shutdown(); } } } Lifecycle Method Description new BRGRegistrationTracker(string name) Create a tracker. The name is used in log messages. bool Initialize() Connect to BRGRenderer.Instance. Returns false if the singleton is unavailable. void Shutdown() Free all tracked chunks, unregister all prototypes, and disconnect. Safe to call multiple times. Property Type Description BRGSystem BRGRenderer The singleton reference. Set after Initialize(), null after Shutdown(). IsRegistered bool true while the tracker is initialized. Name string Display name for log messages. Callbacks You can set callbacks for initialization and shutdown, which is how BRGRegisterer hooks in its OnInitialize / OnShutdown methods: var tracker = new BRGRegistrationTracker("MyTracker"); tracker.InitializeCallback = () => { /* register protos, alloc chunks, etc. */ }; tracker.ShutdownCallback = () => { /* clean up local state only */ }; tracker.Initialize(); // calls InitializeCallback after connecting If InitializeCallback throws, the tracker automatically calls ShutdownCallback and shuts down to prevent partial initialization. Structs InstanceData Per-instance data for registration and updates. Field Type Description position float3 World-space position. rotation quaternion World-space rotation. scale float3 Local scale. signatureIndex int Global signature/prototype index returned by RegisterRenderSignatureFromPrefab or RegisterRenderSignature. color Color32 Per-instance color tint. Requires Enable Per-Instance Color on the Config. PrototypeData The asset definition — meshes, materials, LODs, and other data extracted from a prefab. This is the "what does it look like" data. Accessed via RenderSignature.asset. Field Type Description sourcePrefab GameObject Original prefab (used for identity comparison). mesh Mesh Base mesh (LOD 0). materials Material[] Materials per submesh (LOD 0). lodMeshes Mesh[] Additional LOD meshes (LOD 1+). lodMaterials Material[][] Materials per LOD level. lodScreenSizes float[] Screen relative heights for LOD transitions. lodFadeTransitionWidths float[] Crossfade width per LOD level. lodCastsShadows bool[] Whether each LOD casts shadows. lodMotionVectorModes MotionVectorGenerationMode[] Per-LOD motion vector mode. lodGroupSize float Reference size for LOD calculations. fadeMode LODFadeMode Crossfade mode from LODGroup. percentageFadeMask uint Bit N = LOD N uses percentage fade (SpeedTree). speedTreeRendererID int Renderer instance ID for SpeedTree wind lookup. usesMeshLod bool Unity 6.2+ Mesh LOD instead of separate meshes per level. RenderSignature The full registration unit — combines a PrototypeData asset with render behavior configuration. This is what you pass to RegisterRenderSignature when you need explicit control over render settings. The same prefab can be registered multiple times with different render settings. Deduplication uses both sourcePrefab and a hash of the config fields, so two RenderSignatures with the same prefab but different shadow settings are treated as separate prototypes. Field Type Default Description asset PrototypeData — The mesh/material/LOD data. motionVectorMode MotionVectorGenerationMode — Motion vector generation mode. animateCrossFading bool — Whether to use animated crossfade. maxShadowCascade int 4 Max shadow cascades. minShadowLOD int 0 Minimum LOD for shadow mesh. maxShadowDistance float 0 Max shadow distance, 0 = global. maxShadowCrossfadeCascade int -99 Cascade-specific crossfade control. lodFadeDuration float 0 Animated crossfade duration override. prototypeGroup BRGPrototypeGroup null Optional group for runtime LOD bias and density control. See BRG Prototype Group. enableDistanceDensity bool false Enable per-instance distance density culling. distanceDensityMode DistanceDensityMode ScreenSize ScreenSize or RawDistance. densityStartScreenSize float 2 Screen-size percentage where thinning begins (Screen Size mode). densityStartDistance float 50 Distance where thinning begins (Raw Distance mode). densityEndDistance float 150 Distance where thinning reaches minimum (Raw Distance mode). densityMinFraction float 0 Minimum density fraction at max distance. 0 = cull all; 0.3 = keep 30%. densityFadeWidth float 0.05 Crossfade width for density transitions. layer int 0 GameObject layer. renderingLayerMask uint 0xffffffff URP/HDRP rendering layer mask. Most users can simply call RegisterRenderSignatureFromPrefab(GameObject), which extracts a RenderSignature from the prefab automatically (including any BRG Prototype Extra Data settings). You can also call ExtractRenderSignature(GameObject) to get a RenderSignature without registering it, modify it, and then pass it to RegisterRenderSignature. ChunkLink Handle to an allocated BRG chunk. Tracked for automatic cleanup on shutdown. Includes a generation counter for ABA-safe liveness checks. Member Type Description Id int Internal chunk identifier. Generation int Generation counter — incremented when the chunk slot is reused, so a stale ChunkLink won't accidentally point at a new chunk. IsValid bool true if the chunk was successfully allocated (Id >= 0). IsAlive bool true if the chunk is still allocated and matches its generation. Use this for ABA-safe checks before operating on a stored ChunkLink. NumActivePools int How many pools the chunk currently occupies. GetPoolGlobalIndex(int localIdx) int Global index of the pool at the given local position within the chunk. NumInstancesInPool(int localIdx) int Instance count in the pool at the given local position. Invalid static Sentinel value for an invalid chunk. InstanceLink Handle to a single instance — the chunk it lives in plus its global slot index. The ChunkId may be an overflow chunk, not the primary ChunkLink.Id. InstanceLink is a passive handle — all per-instance operations (move, color, remove, etc.) are performed via methods on the tracker or registerer. See Tracked Staging and Unsafe Direct Modification below. Property Type Description ChunkId int The chunk this instance belongs to (may be an overflow chunk). GlobalBRGSlotIndex int Global slot index in the instance buffer. IsValid bool true if the slot index is >= 0. Invalid static Sentinel value (-1, -1). Render Signature Registration All registrations are tracked and automatically unregistered on Shutdown(). Method Description RenderSignature ExtractRenderSignature(GameObject prefab) Extract a RenderSignature from a prefab without registering it. int RegisterRenderSignatureFromPrefab(GameObject prefab) Register a single signature extracted from the prefab. Returns the global prototype index, or -1 on failure. int[] RegisterRenderSignaturesFromPrefab(GameObject prefab) Register multiple signatures extracted from a prefab that produces more than one (e.g. multi-renderer prefabs). Returns the array of global indices. int RegisterRenderSignature(RenderSignature signature) Register an explicit RenderSignature. Returns the global prototype index, or -1 on failure. void UnregisterRenderSignature(int globalIdx) Manually unregister a single prototype. Removes it from the tracker's auto-cleanup list. Chunk Management All chunks are tracked and automatically freed on Shutdown(). Method Description int MaxInstancesPerChunk Maximum instances a single chunk can hold (driven by Max Pools Per Chunk × 64 in the Config). ChunkLink AllocChunk() Allocate a new chunk. void WriteChunk(ChunkLink, NativeArray<InstanceData>, Bounds, float cullDistance = 0, float instanceCullDistance = float.MaxValue) Write instances to a chunk. Automatically splits across overflow chunks if instance count exceeds MaxInstancesPerChunk. Overflow chunks share bounds with the primary chunk. void ReleaseChunk(ChunkLink) Free a chunk and all its overflow chunks. Idempotent. void RecalculateChunkBounds(ChunkLink, Bounds) Update chunk culling bounds (applies to primary + all overflows). void SetChunkEnabled(ChunkLink, bool) Enable or disable a chunk for rendering (applies to primary + all overflows). Disabled chunks skip culling and rendering. bool GetChunkEnabled(ChunkLink) Returns whether the chunk is currently enabled. void SetRenderEnabled(bool) Enable/disable rendering for ALL chunks owned by this tracker at once. WriteChunk Parameters Parameter Type Default Description link ChunkLink — The chunk to write to. instances NativeArray<InstanceData> — Instance data array. bounds Bounds — World-space AABB used for hierarchical culling. Should tightly enclose all instances. cullDistance float 0 Per-chunk max render distance. 0 = unlimited. instanceCullDistance float float.MaxValue Per-instance max render distance applied during GPU culling. Instance Lifecycle Method Description InstanceLink AddInstance(ChunkLink, InstanceData) Add a single instance. Tries the primary chunk, then existing overflow chunks, then allocates a new overflow if needed. Returns InstanceLink.Invalid on failure or for a stale/freed ChunkLink. InstanceLink[] AddInstances(ChunkLink, NativeArray<InstanceData>, int count) Add multiple instances with automatic overflow. Returns one InstanceLink per added instance. InstanceLink MoveInstanceToChunk(InstanceLink source, ChunkLink dest, InstanceData) Add to destination first, then remove from source. Returns InstanceLink.Invalid if the destination is full — source untouched in that case. Lookups Method Description InstanceLink GetInstanceLink(ChunkLink, int localIndex) Resolve a logical instance index (0..GetTotalChunkInstanceCount − 1, spanning primary + overflow) into a current InstanceLink. Returns InstanceLink.Invalid if the chunk is freed or the index is out of range. int GetTotalChunkInstanceCount(ChunkLink) Total instance count including overflow chunks. int GetOverflowChunkCount(ChunkLink) Number of overflow chunks attached to this primary. void GetPerChunkInstanceCounts(ChunkLink, List<int>) Instance counts per sub-chunk: primary at index 0, then each overflow. Tracked Staging For most use cases, you should use the staged Stage* API. These methods accumulate per-slot writes and merge them so that multiple updates to the same instance within one frame collapse into a single GPU write. The staged changes are flushed automatically during BRGRenderer's next update. Method Description StagePosition(InstanceLink \| int slot, float3) Update position. StageRotation(InstanceLink \| int slot, quaternion) Update rotation. StageScale(InstanceLink \| int slot, float3) Update scale. StageMoveAndRotate(InstanceLink \| int slot, float3, quaternion) Update position and rotation. StageMove(InstanceLink \| int slot, float3, quaternion, float3) Update full TRS. StageColor(InstanceLink \| int slot, Color32) Update per-instance color. StageSetEnabled(InstanceLink \| int slot, bool) Enable or disable a single instance. Disabled instances stay in the buffer but are culled. StageRemove(InstanceLink) / StageRemove(int chunkId, int slot) Remove an instance. Also drops any pending staged writes for that slot. // move + color + enable in one frame -> single merged GPU write tracker.StageMoveAndRotate(link, newPos, newRot); tracker.StageColor(link, Color.red); tracker.StageSetEnabled(link, true); Unsafe Direct Modification The *Unsafe variants are direct pass-throughs to BRGRenderer with no buffering, no merging, and no conflict resolution. Use them only when you know what you're doing — for example, in performance-critical hot paths where you've already deduplicated writes yourself, or when you need writes to land immediately. Method Description SetPositionUnsafe(InstanceLink \| int slot, float3) Direct position write. SetRotationUnsafe(InstanceLink \| int slot, quaternion) Direct rotation write. SetScaleUnsafe(InstanceLink \| int slot, float3) Direct scale write. MoveAndRotateUnsafe(InstanceLink \| int slot, float3, quaternion) Position + rotation. MoveUnsafe(InstanceLink \| int slot, float3, quaternion, float3) Full TRS. SetColorUnsafe(InstanceLink \| int slot, Color32) Direct color write. SetEnabledUnsafe(InstanceLink \| int slot, bool) Direct enable/disable. RemoveUnsafe(InstanceLink) / RemoveUnsafe(int chunkId, int slot) Direct removal. SampleLightProbeUnsafe(InstanceLink \| int slot, float3 position) Re-sample light probes at a position. Mixing staged and unsafe writes on the same slot in the same frame is undefined — pick one path. ChunkWritten Event When WriteChunk is called, the underlying GPU writes may be deferred (e.g. for a buffer resize). The ChunkWritten event fires once per primary chunk after all of its sub-chunks (primary + overflow) have completed their writes, so you can safely call GetInstanceLink afterward. tracker.ChunkWritten += (chunkId) => { var link = tracker.GetInstanceLink(myChunkLink, 0); // cache or modify the instance }; Difference from BRGRegisterer BRGRegisterer is a thin MonoBehaviour wrapper around BRGRegistrationTracker. It adds: Automatic Initialize() on OnEnable, Shutdown() on OnDisable Editor support via [ExecuteAlways] with deferred initialization Abstract OnInitialize() / OnShutdown() hooks via the callback system A virtual OnChunkWritten(int) hook for the ChunkWritten event Protected method forwarding so subclasses don't touch the tracker directly If your registration logic lives in a MonoBehaviour, use Custom Registerer. If it doesn't, use BRGRegistrationTracker directly.

articles/api/system-overview.html.title: System Overview | BRG Instanced Renderer
articles/api/system-overview.html.summary: System Overview This page explains how BRG Instanced Renderer organizes and renders instances internally. Understanding these concepts will help you write effective Custom Registerers and make informed decisions about chunk layout and memory. Prototypes and Render Signatures A prototype is the asset identity for a type of instance — the mesh, materials, LOD meshes, LOD screen sizes, fade mode, and other visual properties extracted from a prefab. Two prefabs that share the same mesh and materials produce the same prototype. A render signature combines a prototype with render behavior configuration — shadow cascade limits, motion vector mode, density settings, crossfade duration, rendering layer mask, and so on. This is the actual registration unit. The same prototype (same prefab) can produce multiple render signatures if registered with different render settings (e.g. different shadow cascades or density modes). When you call RegisterRenderSignatureFromPrefab(prefab), the system extracts both the prototype data and the render config (including any BRG Prototype Extra Data settings), and returns a prototype index — a global integer ID that instances use to reference their render signature. Deduplication uses a hash of both the asset identity and the config, so identical registrations share a single index while the same prefab with different settings gets separate indices. Chunks A chunk is a spatial grouping of instances with shared culling bounds. Chunks are not per-render-signature — a single chunk can contain a mix of instances from any number of different render signatures. Every instance belongs to exactly one chunk, but chunks are allowed to spatially overlap — an instance can exist within the spatial bounds of a different chunk even though it only belongs to one. There is no strict spatial partitioning; chunks are simply logical groupings with a bounding box used for culling. Chunks are the first thing the culling system evaluates. Before testing any individual instance, the system tests the chunk's bounding box against the camera frustum and cull distance. If the entire chunk is outside the frustum or beyond the cull distance, all of its instances are skipped in one operation. This means chunk layout directly affects performance: Spatially tight chunks (instances close together) cull efficiently because the bounding box is small and likely to be entirely inside or outside the frustum. Spatially large chunks produce large bounding boxes that are less likely to be culled at the chunk level, meaning more instances proceed to per-instance GPU culling. This is not a major concern — per-instance culling on the GPU is fast, and processing a few extra instances has negligible impact. Chunk-level culling is an optimization, not a requirement. When a chunk write exceeds the maximum instances per chunk, the system automatically creates overflow chunks and splits the data across them. Overflow chunks share the same culling bounds as the primary chunk, so they are always culled together as a group. This is handled transparently — queries like GetInstanceLink() and GetTotalChunkInstanceCount() aggregate across the primary and overflow chunks automatically. Pools Pools are the memory layer between chunks and individual instances. Like chunks, pools are not per-render-signature — a single pool can hold instances of different signatures. Each pool is a fixed-size block of 64 instance slots in the global GPU buffer. When instances are written to a chunk, the system allocates enough pools to hold them. For example, writing 200 instances allocates 4 pools (256 slots, 200 occupied). Pools are returned to a free list when their chunk is released, and reused by future allocations. For guidance on pool utilization, see Important Tips. Culling Pipeline Every frame, each camera triggers a multi-stage culling pipeline that determines which instances are visible. The pipeline runs in two phases: a CPU pre-pass on chunks, followed by GPU compute passes on individual instances. Burst Job Chunk Culling For each chunk, the system tests: Frustum culling — the chunk's bounding box is tested against the camera's six frustum planes. If the box is entirely outside any plane, the chunk is culled. Distance culling — the closest point on the bounding box to the camera is compared against the chunk's cull distance. If the chunk is too far, it is culled. Baked occlusion culling — if enabled, the system queries Unity's occlusion data to check whether the chunk is hidden behind static geometry. Chunks that survive produce a visibility mask that is uploaded to the GPU for the next stage. GPU Chunk Culling If HZB occlusion culling is enabled, a compute shader performs a hierarchical Z-buffer test on each chunk that passed the Burst job stage. Chunks whose bounding box is fully occluded by closer geometry are culled before any per-instance work begins. GPU Instance Culling A compute shader iterates over the instances in each visible chunk and applies per-instance tests: Density culling — each instance has a deterministic spatial hash. If the hash exceeds the current density scale, the instance is culled. This provides stochastic thinning that is stable across frames. Screen-size culling — the instance's projected screen size is computed from its world-space bounds and distance to the camera. If it falls below the smallest LOD threshold, it is culled entirely. LOD selection — the screen size is compared against the prototype's LOD thresholds to select which mesh to render. If crossfade is active, both the current and target LOD are emitted with a blend factor. HZB occlusion culling — if enabled, the instance's bounds are tested against a hierarchical Z-buffer (a mipmap pyramid of the depth buffer). Instances hidden behind closer geometry are culled. Shadow culling — separate shadow-specific tests compare against per-prototype shadow distances and cascade limits. Surviving instances are sorted into draw buckets grouped by prototype, LOD level, and render pass (main vs. shadow). The system then finalizes indirect draw arguments and dispatches them through Unity's BatchRendererGroup API. Registration to Rendering Putting it all together, the full pipeline from setup to screen is: Register render signatures — extract prototype data and render config from prefabs and assign prototype indices. Allocate chunks — reserve chunk slots for spatial groups of instances. Write instances — fill chunks with instance data (position, rotation, scale, prototype index). The system allocates pools, packs data into GPU buffers, and computes chunk bounds. Per-frame culling — each camera triggers the Burst job chunk cull, then the GPU instance cull. Visible instances are bucketed into indirect draw calls. Rendering — Unity's BatchRendererGroup dispatches the draw calls. Per-instance transforms and properties are read directly from GPU buffers with no CPU involvement.

articles/components/brg-camera-settings..title: BRG Camera Settings | BRG Instanced Renderer
articles/components/brg-camera-settings..summary: BRG Camera Settings An optional component added to cameras to control the LOD bias multiplier for BRG Instanced Renderer on a per-camera basis. Inspector Properties Property Type Default Description LOD Bias Multiplier float (0.01–10) 1.0 A multiplier applied on top of Unity's global QualitySettings.lodBias. How It Works The final LOD bias used for a camera is: Final LOD Bias = QualitySettings.lodBias x LOD Bias Multiplier A multiplier of 1.0 uses the global Quality Settings value as-is (default behavior). A multiplier greater than 1.0 pushes LOD transitions farther away, keeping higher-detail meshes visible at greater distances. A multiplier less than 1.0 pulls LOD transitions closer, using lower-detail meshes sooner. When to Use Cinematic cameras — Set a higher multiplier to maintain maximum detail for cutscenes or beauty shots. Minimap or overview cameras — Set a lower multiplier to aggressively use lower LODs, since detail isn't needed. Split-screen or secondary cameras — Reduce LOD quality on secondary viewports to save rendering budget. Methods SnapCrossfade public void SnapCrossfade() Snaps all animated crossfade transitions to their target LOD for this camera. Convenience wrapper around SnapCrossfadeState on the singleton. // snap crossfade after teleporting this camera GetComponent<BRGCameraSettings>().SnapCrossfade(); Notes If no BRG Camera Settings component is present on a camera, the standard QualitySettings.lodBias is used with a multiplier of 1.0. This component only affects LOD selection within BRG Instanced Renderer. It does not change Unity's built-in LOD behavior for non-BRG objects.

articles/components/brg-gameobject-group.title: BRG GameObject Group | BRG Instanced Renderer
articles/components/brg-gameobject-group.summary: BRG GameObject Group Converts a hierarchy of prefab instances into GPU-instanced rendering via BRG Instanced Renderer. Instances are spatially batched into chunks and serialized, so startup is instant with no runtime transform scanning. For a step-by-step setup guide, see Getting Started: GameObjects. Inspector Properties Property Type Default Description Chunk Mode enum Static (Single Chunk) Controls how instances are spatially organized. See Chunk Modes below. Chunk Size float 50m World-space size of the spatial grid cells. Instances are grouped into chunks based on their position. Affects culling granularity — smaller chunks cull more precisely, larger chunks reduce overhead. Only applies to Static (Multi Chunk) mode. Cull Distance float 0 Maximum render distance in meters. Instances in this group beyond this distance are not rendered. 0 means no distance limit. Show Chunk Gizmos bool true Draws wireframe bounding boxes in the Scene View for each chunk, color-coded by fill percentage. Inspector Actions Button Description Convert Children to Instances Scans all direct children, groups them into spatial chunks, serializes the data, and disables their Mesh Renderers and LOD Groups. Revert to GameObjects Re-enables original Mesh Renderers and LOD Groups, returning to standard Unity rendering. Refresh Rebuilds chunk data from the current state of the source objects. Use after moving, adding, or removing instances. You can also convert arbitrary GameObjects (not just children) via the hierarchy context menu: GameObject > BRG > Convert to BRG Instances. This creates a new BRG GameObject Group and converts the selected objects into it. Status Display When converted, the inspector shows: Converted: Yes/No Chunk Count: Number of spatial chunks Prototype Count: Number of unique prefab types Instance Count: Total instances across all chunks Chunk Modes Static (Single Chunk) — Default All instances go into one chunk with tight bounds that encapsulate them. The Chunk Size setting is ignored. Best for small groups of static instances where spatial sub-chunking would add overhead without meaningful culling benefit. Static (Multi Chunk) Instances are placed into a spatial grid based on their world position and the Chunk Size setting. Each chunk has tight bounding boxes computed at edit time, giving the best culling precision. If a grid cell exceeds the maximum instance capacity (determined by Config pool settings), it is split into multiple chunks. Best for large groups of static instances spread out spatially. Dynamic Global Chunk All instances are placed into a single chunk with world-sized bounds. The Chunk Size setting is ignored. This mode is intended for instances that move frequently at runtime, since the chunk bounds don't need to encapsulate specific positions. Best for instances that move frequently. Use with native transform tracking. Native Transform Tracking Each converted source object gets a BRG GameObject Link component. When a linked GameObject's transform changes, the corresponding BRG instance is automatically updated on the GPU — no manual API calls needed. This uses Unity's native change tracking (ObjectDispatcher) to detect transform changes each frame, making it efficient even with large numbers of tracked objects. Only objects that actually moved are processed. Tip For instances that move at runtime, use Dynamic Global Chunk mode. Static mode computes tight chunk bounds at edit time, which won't account for runtime movement. Clone Support When a converted source object is cloned via Instantiate(), the BRG GameObject Link automatically detects the clone and registers it as a new BRG instance under the same group. The clone inherits the same prototype as the original. Destroying a clone removes its BRG instance automatically. Notes Source GameObjects remain in the hierarchy after conversion. Their renderers are disabled but you can still select and move them. After editing source objects in the editor, click Refresh to update the serialized chunk data. Mixed prefab types under the same parent are fully supported. Each unique prefab becomes a separate prototype.
